subject: Priority engines for real-time inference and evaluation playbook
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <a.turner@pixelpay.com>; Priya Desai <priya.desai@pixelpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priority engines for real-time inference and evaluation playbook

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — appreciate the clear breakdown of PixelPay's 99th-percentile latency requirement for transaction flagging and the tight cost targets for pilot. I promised a concise follow-up with our recommended candidate engines, the operational evaluation plan, and concrete next steps. High-level summary below; full notes and numbers attached.

TL;DR (recommended candidates)
- rw-realtime-13b-q4: best balance for <80ms P50 on RTX A10 with 8-token warmups; low infra cost for pilot.
- rw-llama-70b-int8: highest quality for fraud detection use cases (fewer false positives) but ~2x cost.
- openfast-30b-ffn: cost-efficient fallback for bulk re-runs and batched scoring (good for nightly reconciliation).

Key tradeoffs (short):
- Latency: rw-realtime-13b-q4 hits your target at expected sequence lengths; rw-llama-70b-int8 has higher P95 (we expect ~220–270ms).
- Cost: rw-realtime-13b-q4 is ~0.6 USD per 1k tokens in our hosted baseline; rw-llama-70b-int8 ~1.3 USD per 1k tokens.
- Quality: rw-llama-70b-int8 reduces semantic hallucination on edge cases; we recommend a small eval set (500 examples) to quantify effect on false positive rate.

Attached: engine_candidate_notes.pdf (short rationale), latency_benchmarks_spreadsheet.csv (P50/P95/cost rows), prompt-set-sample.txt (seed prompts we used).

Next steps I propose:
1) Lightweight eval: we run the 500-example quality and latency sweep on your sample set (Redwood provides results + regression metrics) — 5 business days.
2) Production pilot config: start with rw-realtime-13b-q4 on Dedicated capacity; can add rw-llama-70b-int8 as canary for high-risk flows.
3) Procurement: we sync with your procurement contact (Priya) to map timelines and PO triggers.

Available for a 30-min check-in tomorrow (Mon) 10:00–11:30 PT or Tue 14:00–16:00 PT — what works?

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the crisp summary. A couple quick clarifications before we schedule the eval: 

1) For the rw-realtime-13b-q4 numbers, can you confirm the sequence length distribution used for the P50/P95 (we have a lot of short prompts with 12–18 tokens but some context).
2) On the rw-llama-70b-int8 quality claim — do you have an example where it meaningfully reduced false positives versus the 13b model? Any concrete prompt examples would help the fraud team.
3) Cost math: is the per-1k token cost you listed including network overhead and KV cache hit assumptions? We need an apples-to-apples for our finance team.

If you can reply with those three data points I can loop in our procurement lead and lock a time. Prefer Mon 10:30 PT if that works for you.

—Alex
Product Lead, PixelPay

Subject: Re: Priority engines for real-time inference and evaluation playbook

Alex — good questions. Quick answers and links below.

1) Sequence length assumptions
- We used a tri-modal distribution based on your transcript: 60% short (12–20 tokens), 30% mid (40–60 tokens), 10% long (>120 tokens). For rw-realtime-13b-q4 the P50 is ~72ms and P95 ~145ms under that mix on a single A10 GPU with our continuous-batching setting. See latency_benchmarks_spreadsheet.csv (tab "seq-dist-weights").

2) Quality example (rw-llama-70b-int8 vs rw-realtime-13b-q4)
- Prompt (seed): "Flag attempts that mention chargebacks or account takeover language but include legitimate dispute reasons."
- 13b candidate: flagged several merchant dispute templates as suspicious (false positives) when wording matched earlier fraud templates.
- 70b int8 candidate: applied better context disambiguation and suppressed false positives for 7/12 edge prompts in our seed set. Full diff is in engine_candidate_notes.pdf (section 3).

3) Cost assumptions
- Values I cited include expected network and 5–8% KV cache-hit uplift (so they are slightly conservative). Per-1k-token numbers assume sustained throughput at pilot scale (50 rps). See spreadsheet (tab "cost-model"). If you want a pure compute-only baseline we can drop the network assumptions — I put both numbers in the sheet.

Operational notes and guardrails
- Regression guard: we will run a zero-downgrade check — any candidate that increases false positives by >2% on the eval set is blocked from canary.
- Canary plan: 1% traffic with live logging + automatic fallback to the 13b candidate on anomaly.
- Prompt hygiene: we recommend a strict templating layer for the fraud flow to keep prefix variance low (reduces P95 tail variance). Sample prompt-set-sample.txt attached.

Next steps (concrete)
A) We run the 500-example quality + latency sweep (Redwood). Deliverable: csv with P50/P95, FP/FN deltas, and a regression decision. Timeline: 5 business days after sample delivery.
B) Procurement sync: Priya — can you confirm procurement cadence and whether we should route an SOW or an MSA + PO?
C) Schedule check-in: Monday 10:30 PT works on our side — I'll send an invite.

If helpful, Ben can join the procurement portion to speed approvals — adding him now.

—Marissa
